avoid: Do not use if as a catch-all control mechanism.
If a condition is really deciding applicability, admission, or routing, move it into guards, gates, or a higher structural choice instead.
conditional_roles.rule: Use each conditional surface for its own job: guards handle applicability and early rejection, gates handle whether a path or step may run at all, and if handles local behavioral variation inside an already-valid path.

gh_pr_merge_guidance: GitHub async merge: gh.pr observes head/base/test-merge identity and stack_state (standalone/stacked/unknown) plus stack; gh.pr.checks observes CI evidence. gh.pr.merge requires expected_head_sha from the accepted CI head, never a freshly fetched replacement. For gh.pr.merge and gh.pr.merge.request, repository is optional: a valid explicit OWNER/REPO overrides the bootstrapped connector_contexts.gh.repository; omitted or null uses that context. Malformed explicit values fail without fallback, and no resolved repository is an error. For checks on candidate M with verified base B and head H, submit expected_head_sha=H, not M. The first version rejects stacked PRs and unknown scope before submission; there is no atomic base or stack guarantee. Save the action result request_id UUID for gh.pr.merge.request: accepted submission is not completion. Observe pending/merged/failed/enqueued once; unavailable is not failed and enqueued is not merged. Only an exact matching existing request is reusable. No polling, queue administration, or admin bypass is provided. GitHub automatic issue closing and branch configuration effects are outside this action. Inspect connector.gh.pr.merge and connector.gh.pr.merge.request for the verified canonical workflow example.
graph_parameters: Structural graph indices can be symbolic parameters of one logical state family. Families are owned by a playbook state declaration, not matching role names across unrelated stores. Profile-backed locations are family instances; different concrete profile files do not by themselves prevent a conditional template link. Fixed disjoint indices and fixed disjoint stores do not match. Access addresses retain concrete store/key proof and add family and selector origin metadata. structural_links separately publish relation_category, selector_correspondence and requirements such as selector_equal, same_family_instance and read_shape_available. Shared mutable selection origins establish parameter correspondence, never equality of values across invocations; independent input scopes require equality too. Used let aliases and forwarded call arguments preserve known origins, while nested store overrides retain their own declaration scope. structural_components and structural_loop_components retain conditional family topology; summary can place consumers with parametric coverage and render state[parameter], without relabeling possible concrete identity as proven. Parent replacement/deletion and read-shape conditions remain explicit. Bootstrap stays separate. A single text note states the matching-selector/instance/read-shape requirement. Concrete links, next, execution and actual-file storage validation retain their existing semantics.
graph_context: Static graph loads declared profile metadata without activation, probes or state reads. Known literal/input/let switches and workflow.profile bindings merge profile inputs using runtime protection rules; workflow defaults and explicit CLI/entry values survive. Explicit CLI profile authority is retained through playbook pre_run. Supported unbound calls propagate profile context; bound caller/callee scopes retain runtime isolation. Working directories follow profile context, while root playbook state locations retain their launch-time binding. Unknown selections preserve fixed inputs and bounded candidate keys instead of clearing all context. Constant maps, lookup and symbolic item/key domains retain up to 32 alternatives without unrolling bodies; no arbitrary expression evaluator or external issue-body inference is added. Accesses publish phase (bootstrap/body), profile and working_directory; boundaries distinguish context uncertainty from unknown structure. Detailed links and components retain bootstrap evidence; business_components and summary reader placement use body links. summary.bootstrap retains launch accesses and bootstrap-only workflows, with a compact JSON pointer in text. Profile uncertainty does not suppress proven fixed-address relations. key_candidates are possible address domains, not equal runtime values; summary may aggregate the same finite domain while keeping identity unresolved. Check, review, plan, run, explain and next are unchanged.
graph_source_placement: Business placement uses existing body read sites and body handoff links. JSON retains per-field joins, alternatives, conditional source availability, unknown coverage and incomplete-reader evidence without choosing a newest writer. Catch/fallback reads remain accounted for without becoming mandatory runtime requirements. Pure alternatives have after=null and render as standalone rows, retaining every candidate in JSON; they are not unresolved. Unique-source readers stay nested. Joins and join_with_alternatives retain their existing layout anchors, not execution prerequisites. Standalone alternatives use category/authored order around intact anchored blocks when compatible; conflicting category bounds preserve anchors and fall back to authored root-row order. Optional workflow category is display metadata only. Unresolved consumers are listed separately. Consumers may perform external effects. Logical store bindings and keys identify contexts; ambiguous stores retain short path qualifiers, while unknown key expressions stay in JSON. Graph v1 retains its detailed fields and adds profile/bootstrap provenance. Known bindings refine address evidence; next remains unchanged.
graph_presentation: Default graph retains its workflow tree and adds trailing state-effect parentheses to mutating workflows. The single legend is: + writes, − deletes, ? conditional; branches show data use, not execution order. + means a write, not guaranteed first creation. Whole-context deletion is −context; partial deletion names the field. Effects retain first-seen field order and deduplicate by context, operation and field. Existing local if, iteration, short-circuit or conditional-gate controls mark ?; duplicate effects under different conditions also keep ?. No unconditional coverage is inferred across guards. Ordinary guard/gate admission alone is not a readiness claim and does not mark every effect conditional. Context qualifiers distinguish ambiguous targets. Read-only-state users have no effect parentheses; business placement separates bootstrap evidence from body dependencies. Expressions, joins, source identities and full evidence stay in --json; summary is additive and retains bootstrap provenance. Grouped writes are not atomic. Ties within a category follow playbook order. Dependency anchors take precedence; anchored blocks retain their order, without category-driven graph links or execution precedence. The graph bundle verifies exact default tree text.
graph_guidance: ordo-playbook graph builds static possible processes from ordered persistent-state access occurrences, independently of next activation and ranking. JSON uses schema ordo.static-process-graph, schema_version 1, replacing the old next-shaped graph output. It publishes workflows, accesses, order_edges, links, components, possible_loop_components, boundaries, and activity.status=not_requested. Store identity is a normalized declared path, not an inode or filesystem-alias proof; keys resolve only from safe static literals/input/let bindings. Same-named dynamic inputs across workflows are not proven equal. Handoffs and invalidations are possible execution even when address identity is proven; parent replacement, subtree deletion and possible empty-parent prune are explicit. Conditions remain symbolic, known calls compose, repeats retain one symbolic body, and unresolved or recursive calls have explicit boundaries. Used let bindings expand at use sites; registered values do not reread storage. Missing state, inputs or probes never remove loaded structure. No state contents, probes or effects are evaluated. Components and potential loops do not prove reachability or executable cycles, infer business stages, or group by file/category/field. Use next for current recommendations; check, review, plan, run, explain, next and actual-file write-before-last-read validation are unchanged.

execution_concepts.check_unknown: Inspect allowed_state, analysis_complete, incomplete_reasons, and unevaluated_relevant_guards. allowed false can mean unknown, not blocked; missing_facts is not inferred from unevaluated expressions.
execution_concepts.state_boundary: Nested analysis does not defer state. A reached run/loop after deferral halts with state_deferral_invocation_barrier; profiles cannot resume it. Cross-invocation and cross-iteration guarantees remain deferred.
execution_concepts.state_deferral: Top-level check defers effectful state writes/deletes after conditions and gates and continues to independent guards, without mutation, simulation, outputs, registers, or reuse. Plan retains ordered non-reusable nodes; run executes admitted mutations once.

failure_diagnostics.rule: When runtime has external command or remote-system context, user-facing diagnostics should distinguish that external cause from workflow or engine logic failures.

purpose: World map for Ordo discovery and authoring bootstrap

recommended_next_calls.purpose: Scan workflow features, named surfaces, and when to use them
Learn preferred workflow rules, including paired check/review passes
Inspect public launch commands, flags, and distinct check/review roles
Inspect which public handles do and do not publish canonical verified snippets

gh_pr_create_guidance: GitHub creation: gh.pr.create requires head, base, title, and an explicit boolean draft; body defaults to empty. repository is optional: valid explicit OWNER/REPO overrides connector_contexts.gh.repository; omitted or null uses context, malformed explicit input fails without fallback. head_repository is a full source OWNER/REPO, default target repository; explicit cross-repository intent requires it, with no fork guessing. head_owner is an optional consistency assertion, otherwise derived from the exact source repository. Same-organization head_repo API argument is derived repository NAME. Reject same-branch/same-repository requests. The action uses ctx.call('gh.pr.list', inputs=...) with resolved repository/head/head_owner/base and state: open; require complete traversal and exact case-insensitive head_repository_key identity. One exact open match including draft returns non-OK already_exists with pull_number, url, created=false and no POST; multiple matches return ambiguous; unknown identity and list failure return precheck_failed. No existing match permits one POST. Only validated HTTP 201 means created=true; malformed 201, timeout, or server failure returns creation_unknown with created=null. HTTP 422 is generic create_refused, not universal duplicate evidence; preserve API errors. No POST retry or automatic readback reconciliation. This is not find-or-reuse or closed-history policy: workflow-owned gh.pr.list state: all classification precedes create's separate open check. Concurrent duplicates can race the check: no atomic uniqueness or exactly-once guarantee. No CI waiting, merge, push, fork, branch cleanup, or extra issue/project operations. Inspect connector.gh.pr.create.
connector_authoring_guidance: Connector-author SDK: ctx.call(name, *, inputs=None) supports nonempty already-resolved inputs only for same-family probe dependencies. Full references (gh.pr.list) and local dotted names (pr.list) work; values are not reevaluated as expressions or templates. Omitted inputs or None preserve legacy no-input behavior. Cross-family calls and probe-to-action hidden mutation are rejected; no new action composition. Inspect connector.authoring for dependency boundaries and verified examples.
gh_pr_list_guidance: GitHub candidate discovery: gh.pr.list observes a full filtered REST pull-request collection, not the search index. repository is optional with the standard connector_contexts.gh.repository default and explicit OWNER/REPO override. state is required: open|closed|all. Prefer state: all for find/create-oriented inspection, optionally narrowed by head/head_owner/base. head_owner is the head repository owner (user or organization), not PR author, and requires head; owner plus branch is not exact repository identity. Compare returned head_repository for exact fork matching. Internal pagination has no public page/cursor/limit; incomplete traversal fails. head with head_owner composes server owner:branch; bare head is matched exactly locally across all state/base pages because GitHub does not guarantee bare-head filtering. Missing head_ref for local filtering fails. The 100-page ceiling applies before local filtering. GitHub.com only, matching bootstrap authentication. Full traversal is not an atomic snapshot or a total remote count guarantee. Empty success means no matches within the supplied filters; one result is a candidate, not automatically the correct PR. Workflow rules classify none, one open, multiple open, and closed history; unknown facts block dependent decisions. Closed/merged history may require additional workflow rules. Listing does not authorize creation, reopening, or merge. gh.pr reads detailed facts by pull_number; gh.pr.create is a separate action with its own mandatory open check. Inspect connector.gh.pr.list for canonical filtered classification fragments.

passes.purpose: Validate workflow applicability and execution readiness

workflow_check_review_passes.rule: Use both check and review after adding or changing a workflow; neither replaces the other.
